title: Selective computation boundary: can a static persistent candidate universe be routed through bounded R before execution?
question: With a fixed candidate universe reused across many queries, does the hardened runtime preserve capability while router candidate work is bounded by the retained subset rather than H?
hypothesis: For the controlled equality relation, an exact content-addressed index can preserve task success while changing actual router input size from H to at most K after a one-time index build. The measurement establishes the runtime boundary and its accounting, not semantic retrieval or the full PLM economic-scaling claim.

arms.name: exhaustive
arms.intervention: score the full persistent candidate universe

arms.name: indexed
arms.intervention: content-address the persistent candidate universe and route only the retained bucket

endpoints.name: success_rate
endpoints.role: primary — task capability over the static candidate universe
endpoints.description: Exact task success using the same hidden world truth and evaluator.

endpoints.name: router_candidates_per_step
endpoints.role: secondary — actual number of candidates presented to the router per query

endpoints.name: index_build_candidates
endpoints.role: secondary — one-time candidate items processed to build the index

endpoints.name: address_query_positions
endpoints.role: secondary — marked positions inspected during query-time addressing

endpoints.name: amortized_candidate_work
endpoints.role: secondary — (one-time build + query addressing + router candidates) / number of queries

decision_rule.condition: indexed success_rate remains within the exhaustive arm's seed spread while router_candidates_per_step is bounded by K and the index is built once per static population
decision_rule.licenses: the hardened runtime has a functioning selective-computation boundary for this controlled relation and the reported retained-set cost is real rather than hypothetical.
decision_rule.does_not_license: semantic retrieval quality, learned addressing, or the L4 economic-scaling claim C5.

decision_rule.condition: indexed success_rate is materially below exhaustive at the same H and K
decision_rule.licenses: the exact address control loses capability under the tested budget.
decision_rule.does_not_license: that selective computation or cheap addressing is impossible.

decision_rule.condition: router_candidates_per_step still grows with H in the indexed arm
decision_rule.licenses: the retrieval boundary is not actually selective in the runtime path.

held_constant: candidate universe is built once per (seed,H) and reused across all queries
the relation is equality on two public marked positions
candidate validity is multiple-valid: every exact signature bucket is acceptable
the same deterministic router, executor, verifier and evaluator are used in both arms
the index never receives hidden acceptable actions or hidden world truth
one-time index construction is reported separately and amortized over exactly 100 queries
this is a control measurement, not evidence for semantic retrieval or full C5
